title: Stochastic target-based scaling safety matrix and governor
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Dedicated fleets need scaling behavior that simultaneously meets throughput guarantees and respects cost and stability budgets. Current autoscalers either react to single-point signals (e.g., p95 or RPS) or allow aggressive surge steps that risk noisy-neighbor and thrash behavior across tenants. This ticket designs and implements a policy engine that constructs a stochastic safety matrix from observed metric distributions and enforces a governor that converts target metrics into safe scaling actions.

Goal: Deliver a conservative-by-default autoscaling policy engine that: 1) consumes multiple target metrics (latency percentiles, token/sec per GPU, queue depth, headroom credits), 2) synthesizes a probabilistic safety envelope (e.g., 95th percentile headroom), 3) drives a hybrid scaling algorithm (dual-loop rate + credit-aware stepper), and 4) enforces fleet-level constraints (max replica delta, tenant fairshare, cooldowns).

Outcomes: Reduced scaling-induced SLO regressions during bursts, predictable cost exposure for reserved capacity customers, and clear guardrails for canary/experimental scaling strategies.
acceptance_criteria: New policy DSL supports specifying multiple target metrics and a safety percentile (e.g., p95 headroom) as strings.
Controller implements dual-loop algorithm: fast reactive loop (rate-limited immediate steps) + slow smoothing loop (quantile-based forecast) and is configurable via runtime flags.
Safety matrix enforces at least: max_delta_replicas per 10m, tenant_min_fairshare, global_max_replicas, and cooldown windows. Values are configurable per fleet.
End-to-end integration tests simulate burst traffic and show reduced oscillations vs baseline autoscaler: p95 latency improvement >= 15% and fewer scale-up/scale-down cycles in 30m window.
Dashboards surface headroom credit usage, safety limit hits, and predicted vs actual scale decisions.
Rolling rollout on dedicated canary fleet with automatic rollback if safety limits triggered >3 times in 1h.
Documentation and operator runbook describing tuning knobs and failure modes are published to Confluence.
notes: Design constrained by existing quota/commit APIs in dedicated backend; we must not change commit accounting during initial rollout.
We will implement safety matrix as a stateless config + short-lived runtime signals; persistent state limited to headroom credit ledger which already exists.
Prefer explicit, simple defaults over opaque heuristics for first rollout to aid debugging by SREs and customer success.
Will coordinate with Console team to add a 'safety hits' visualization and per-fleet limit editor.
Estimate assumes availability of historical per-fleet percentiles from telemetry pipeline (see dependencies).
decisions: Decision: Use a hybrid algorithm (fast reactive + slow forecast) instead of purely predictive ML during initial rollout. Rationale: lower blast radius, easier to reason about, requires no new model infra.

Decision: Target metrics set to configurable list in policy DSL. Default set: p95 latency, tokens_per_gpu_1m, queue_depth_1m, headroom_credit_pct. Rationale: these collectively map to user-perceived SLOs and internal capacity signals.
Decision: Safety percentile defaulted to 95 (stochastic safety matrix at p95). Operators can choose p99 for conservative fleets. Rationale: balances false positives and cost for most workloads.

Decision: Enforce global rate limits on scaling actions: max_delta_replicas=+/-3 per 10m and cool_down=120s. Rationale: prevents large oscillatory steps that corrput utilization and billing predictability.
Decision: Implement tenant fairshare by subtracting guaranteed reserved capacity before evaluating headroom credits to avoid penalizing reserved tenants.
Decision: Expose policy as JSON/YAML in control plane with validation schema to prevent misconfiguration.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Deploy to 5 non-production dedicated fleets, monitor for 72h, metrics: scale cycles, p95 latency, cost delta.
Phase 2 (Beta): Enable for small set of production fleets with permissive defaults and supervised rollback for 7 days.
Phase 3 (GA): Enable for all dedicated fleets and expose tuning UI in Console; announce migration window and opt-in policy templates.
Rollback criteria: >3 safety_limit triggers in 1h OR sustained p95 latency degradation >10% for 30m OR increase in scale churn beyond baseline by 30%.
checklist: Implement policy DSL schema and validation
Implement dual-loop controller and safety enclosure
Unit and integration tests for safety matrix enforcement
Add Console telemetry panels and limit editor
Write operator runbook and tuning guide
